title: Find the shapes no approved message has

blocks.text: One approved message is a thin reference. Approved purchases differ among themselves: some cards have 19 digits, some terminals send an expiry date and others don't. Compared with one of them, a rejected purchase can show differences that the host accepts every day.

So the support desk keeps the morning's approved purchases from the same release, and `Shapes.unseen(approved, rejected)` lists the fields of a rejected message whose shape none of them has. `unseen` is written. Finish the two methods marked `TODO` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/Shapes.java`:

items: `shape(...)`: one field described in one of the forms the comment above it lists;
`seen(...)`: every description a field has across the approved messages.

blocks.text: About twelve lines in total. Some tests' messages carry a PIN block, which is binary.

cases.says: a field missing from the rejected message, or of another length, is reported when no approved message has it that way
values that differ as two purchases differ (card, amount, STAN, time, terminal) are not reported
a letter in place of a digit is reported although the length is unchanged
an accented letter is outside printable ASCII and is reported, although Java counts it as a letter
a binary field is compared by its length in bytes, not by the hex text of its value
a shape that any one approved message has is not reported, so the comparison is with all of them
a field absent from the rejected message is not reported when some approved message lacked it too

origin.section: 15.2. A Rejected Message Is Compared With Approved Ones by the Shape of Each Field

concepts: A rejected message is compared with approved ones by each field's presence, length and kind of characters, because values differ between any two purchases.
The comparison is with approved messages of the same release and kind of purchase, and a shape any of them has is not a fault.
